(8) “document” means any matter expressed or described upon any substance by means of letters, 
figures or marks, or by more than one of those means, and includes electronic and digital record, 
intended to be used, or which may be used, as evidence of that matter. 
Explanation 1.—It is immaterial by what means or upon what substance the letters, figures or 
marks are formed, or whether the evidence is intended for, or may be used in a Court or not. 
(a) A writing expressing the terms of a contract, which may be used as evidence of the contract, 
is a document. 
(b) A cheque upon a banker is a document. 
(c) A power-of-attorney is a document. 
(d) A map or plan which is intended to be used or which may be used as evidence, is a document. 
(e) A writing containing directions or instructions is a document. 
Explanation 2.—Whatever is expressed by means of letters, figures or marks as explained by 
mercantile or other usage, shall be deemed to be expressed by such letters, figures or marks within 
the meaning of this section, although the same may not be actually expressed. 
A writes his name on the back of a bill of exchange payable to his order. The meaning of the 
endorsement, as explained by mercantile usage, is that the bill is to be paid to the holder. The 
endorsement is a document, and shall be construed in the same manner as if the words “pay to the 
holder” or words to that effect had been written over the signature; 
(9) “fraudulently” means doing anything with the intention to defraud but not otherwise;

(ii) in the service or pay of a local authority as defined in clause (31) of section 3 of 
the General Clauses Act, 1897 (10 of 1897), a corporation established by or under a 
Central or State Act or a Government company as defined in clause (45) of section 2 of 
the Companies Act, 2013 (18 of 2013). 
Explanation.— 
(a) persons falling under any of the descriptions made in this clause are public servants, 
whether appointed by the Government or not; 
(b) every person who is in actual possession of the situation of a public servant, whatever 
legal defect there may be in his right to hold that situation is a public servant; 
(c) “election” means an election for the purpose of selecting members of any legislative, 
municipal or other public authority, of whatever character, the method of selection to which 
is by, or under any law for the time being in force. 
 A Municipal Commissioner is a public servant; 
(29) “reason to believe”.—A person is said to have “reason to believe” a thing, if he has 
sufficient cause to believe that thing but not otherwise; 
(30) “special law” means a law applicable to a particular subject; 
(31) “valuable security” means a document which is, or purports to be, a document whereby any 
legal right is created, extended, transferred, restricted, extinguished or released, or whereby any 
person acknowledges that he lies under legal liability, or has not a certain legal right.

(4) In every Part of this Sanhita, except where a contrary intention appears from the context, words 
which refer to acts done extend also to illegal omissions. 
(5) When a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, 
each of such persons is liable for that act in the same manner as if it were done by him alone. 
(6) Whenever an act, which is criminal only by reason of its being done with a criminal knowledge or 
intention, is done by several persons, each of such persons who joins in the act with such knowledge or 
intention is liable for the act in the same manner as if the act were done by him alone with that knowledge 
or intention. 
(7) Wherever the causing of a certain effect, or an attempt to cause that effect, by an act or by an 
omission, is an offence, it is to be understood that the causing of that effect partly by an act and partly by 
an omission is the same offence. 
A intentionally causes Z’s death, partly by illegally omitting to give Z food, and partly by beating Z. 
A has committed murder. 
(8) When an offence is committed by means of several acts, whoever intentionally cooperates in the 
commission of that offence by doing any one of those acts, either singly or jointly with any other person, 
commits that offence. 
(a) A and B agree to murder Z by severally and at different times giving him small doses of poison. 
A and B administer the poison according to the agreement with intent to murder Z. Z dies from the 
effects the several doses of poison so administered to him. Here A and B intentionally cooperate in the 
commission of murder and as each of them does an act by which the death is caused, they are both guilty 
of the offence though their acts are separate. 
(b) A and B are joint jailors, and as such have the charge of Z, a prisoner, alternatively for six hours 
at a time. A and B, intending to cause Z’s death, knowingly cooperate in causing that effect by illegally 
omitting, each during the time of his attendance, to furnish Z with food supplied to them for that purpose. 
Z dies of hunger. Both A and B are guilty of the murder of Z. 
(c) A, a jailor, has the charge of Z, a prisoner. A, intending to cause Z’s death, illegally omits to 
supply Z with food; in consequence of which Z is much reduced in strength, but the starvation is not 
sufficient to cause his death. A is dismissed from his office, and B succeeds him. B, without collusion or 
cooperation with A, illegally omits to supply Z with food, knowing that he is likely thereby to cause Z’s 
death. Z dies of hunger. B is guilty of murder, but, as A did not cooperate with B. A is guilty only of an 
attempt to commit murder. 
(9) Where several persons are engaged or concerned in the commission of a criminal act, they may be 
guilty of different offences by means of that act. 
A attacks Z under such circumstances of grave provocation that his killing of Z would be only 
culpable homicide not amounting to murder. B, having ill-will towards Z and intending to kill him, and 
not having been subject to the provocation, assists A in killing Z. Here, though A and B are both engaged 
in causing Z’s death, B is guilty of murder, and A is guilty only of culpable homicide.

Dishonestly breaking open receptacle containing property.—(1) Whoever dishonestly or 
with intent to commit mischief, breaks open or unfastens any closed receptacle which contains or which 
he believes to contain property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term 
(2) Whoever, being entrusted with any closed receptacle which contains or which he believes to 
contain property, without having authority to open the same, dishonestly, or with intent to commit 
mischief, breaks open or unfastens that receptacle, shall be punished with imprisonment of either 
description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

possession of another with intent to commit an offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy any person in 
possession of such property or having lawfully entered into or upon such property, unlawfully remains 
there with intent thereby to intimidate, insult or annoy any such person or with intent to commit an 
offence is said to commit criminal trespass. 
(2) Whoever commits criminal trespass by entering into or remaining in any building, tent or vessel 
used as a human dwelling or any building used as a place for worship, or as a place for the custody of 
property, is said to commit house-trespass. 
Explanation.—The introduction of any part of the criminal trespasser’s body is entering sufficient to 
constitute house-trespass. 
(3) Whoever commits criminal trespass shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for 
a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with 
(4) Whoever commits house-trespass shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a 
term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.

House-trespass in order to commit offence.—Whoever commits house-trespass in order to the 
committing of any offence— 
(a) punishable with death, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous 
imprisonment for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; 
(b) punishable with imprisonment for life, shall be punished with imprisonment of either 
description for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; 
(c) punishable with imprisonment, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for 
a term which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine: 
Provided that if the offence intended to be committed is theft, the term of the imprisonment may be 
extended to seven years.

House-trespass after preparation for hurt, assault or wrongful restraint.—Whoever 
commits house-trespass, having made preparation for causing hurt to any person or for assaulting any 
person, or for wrongfully restraining any person, or for putting any person in fear of hurt, or of assault, or 
of wrongful restraint, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may

Abettor.—A person abets an offence, who abets either the commission of an offence, or the 
commission of an act which would be an offence, if committed by a person capable by law of committing 
an offence with the same intention or knowledge as that of the abettor. 
Explanation 1.—The abetment of the illegal omission of an act may amount to an offence although 
the abettor may not himself be bound to do that act. 
Explanation 2.—To constitute the offence of abetment it is not necessary that the act abetted should 
be committed, or that the effect requisite to constitute the offence should be caused. 
(a) A instigates B to murder C. B refuses to do so. A is guilty of abetting B to commit murder. 
(b) A instigates B to murder D. B in pursuance of the instigation stabs D. D recovers from the wound. 
A is guilty of instigating B to commit murder. 
Explanation 3.—It is not necessary that the person abetted should be capable by law of committing 
an offence, or that he should have the same guilty intention or knowledge as that of the abettor, or any 
guilty intention or knowledge. 
(a) A, with a guilty intention, abets a child or a person of unsound mind to commit an act which 
would be an offence, if committed by a person capable by law of committing an offence, and having the 
same intention as A. Here A, whether the act be committed or not, is guilty of abetting an offence. 
(b) A, with the intention of murdering Z, instigates B, a child under seven years of age, to do an act 
which causes Z’s death. B, in consequence of the abetment, does the act in the absence of A and thereby 
causes Z’s death. Here, though B was not capable by law of committing an offence, A is liable to be 
punished in the same manner as if B had been capable by law of committing an offence, and had 
committed murder, and he is therefore subject to the punishment of death. 
(c) A instigates B to set fire to a dwelling-house. B, in consequence of his unsoundness of mind, 
being incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is wrong or contrary to law, sets 
fire to the house in consequence of A’s instigation. B has committed no offence, but A is guilty of 
abetting the offence of setting fire to a dwelling-house, and is liable to the punishment provided for that 
(d) A, intending to cause a theft to be committed, instigates B to take property belonging to Z out of 
Z’s possession. A induces B to believe that the property belongs to A. B takes the property out of Z’s 
possession, in good faith, believing it to be A’s property. B, acting under this misconception, does not 
take dishonestly, and therefore does not commit theft. But A is guilty of abetting theft, and is liable to the 
same punishment as if B had committed theft. 
Explanation 4.—The abetment of an offence being an offence, the abetment of such an abetment is 
also an offence. 
A instigates B to instigate C to murder Z. B accordingly instigates C to murder Z, and C commits that 
offence in consequence of B’s instigation. B is liable to be punished for his offence with the punishment 
for murder; and, as A instigated B to commit the offence, A is also liable to the same punishment. 
Explanation 5.—It is not necessary to the commission of the offence of abetment by conspiracy that 
the abettor should concert the offence with the person who commits it. It is sufficient if he engages in the 
conspiracy in pursuance of which the offence is committed.

A concerts with B a plan for poisoning Z. It is agreed that A shall administer the poison. B then 
explains the plan to C mentioning that a third person is to administer the poison, but without mentioning 
A’s name. C agrees to procure the poison, and procures and delivers it to B for the purpose of its being 
used in the manner explained. A administers the poison; Z dies in consequence. Here, though A and C 
have not conspired together, yet C has been engaged in the conspiracy in pursuance of which Z has been 
murdered. C has therefore committed the offence defined in this section and is liable to the punishment 
for murder.

A complaint has been filed under Section 304, read with Section 305 and Section 307, for the commission of Disorderly Conduct Causing Disturbance in Public Place, Use of Obscene Language in Public, and Obscene Act in Public View, respectively, at a railway station. The complainant has also prayed to invoke provisions of Section 53 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), arrest and detention of the accused, and to conduct an inquest under Section 176 of BNSS. Furthermore, the complainant has requested inspection of CCTV footage and examination of passengers who witnessed the incident as potential witnesses.

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 304], [BNS Section 305], [BNS Section 307], [BNS Section 353], [BNS Section 355]

## Recommendation / next steps
Based on the complaint, the police should investigate the incident and gather evidence to establish the identity and culpability of the accused. The complainant's request to inspect the CCTV footage and examine passengers who witnessed the incident should be considered. The police may also consider invoking provisions of Section 53 of BNSS for the arrest and detention of the accused, and conducting an inquest under Section 176 of BNSS to ascertain the facts and circumstances of the incident.

Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found.

of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.—Whoever fails to appear at the specified place and the specified time as 
required by a proclamation published under sub-section (1) of section 84 of the Bharatiya Nagarik 
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, 
or with fine, or with both, or with community service, and where a declaration has been made under 
sub-section (4) of that section pronouncing him as a proclaimed offender, he shall be punished with 
imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

Statements conducing to public mischief.—(1) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any 
statement, false information, rumour, or report, including through electronic means— 
(a) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the 
Army, Navy or Air Force of India to mutiny or otherwise disregard or fail in his duty as such; or 
(b) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, fear or alarm to the public, or to any section

shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

rumour or alarming news, including through electronic means, with intent to create or promote, or which 
is likely to create or promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or

religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with 
imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed

against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been

section 64, section 65, section 66, section 67, section 68, section 70, section 71, section 74,

shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but 
which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine.

(a) does any obscene act in any public place; or 
(b) sings, recites or utters any obscene song, ballad or words, in or near any public place, 
shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, 
or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration.—(1) Whoever, by words either 
spoken or written or by signs or by visible representations or through electronic communication or 
otherwise,— 
(a) makes or publishes any imputation that any class of persons cannot, by reason of their being 
members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, bear true faith 
and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established or uphold the sovereignty and 
integrity of India; or

(b) asserts, counsels, advises, propagates or publishes that any class of persons shall, by reason of 
their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, be 
denied, or deprived of their rights as citizens of India; or 
(c) makes or publishes any assertion, counsel, plea or appeal concerning the obligation of any 
class of persons, by reason of their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional 
group or caste or community, and such assertion, counsel, plea or appeal causes or is likely to cause 
disharmony or feelings of enmity or hatred or ill-will between such members and other persons; or 
(d) makes or publishes false or misleading information, jeopardising the sovereignty, unity and 
integrity or security of India, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (1) in any place of worship or in any 
assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished 
with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.

OF OFFENCES BY OR RELATING TO PUBLIC SERVANTS

Misconduct in public by a drunken person.—Whoever, in a state of intoxication, appears in 
any public place, or in any place which it is a trespass in him to enter, and there conducts himself in such 
a manner as to cause annoyance to any person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term 
which may extend to twenty-four hours, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with 
both or with community service.

various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

statement, false information, rumour, or report, including through electronic means— 
(a) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the 
Army, Navy or Air Force of India to mutiny or otherwise disregard or fail in his duty as such; or 
(b) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, fear or alarm to the public, or to any section 
of the public whereby any person may be induced to commit an offence against the State or against 
the public tranquillity; or 
(c) with intent to incite, or which is likely to incite, any class or community of persons to commit 
any offence against any other class or community, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

rumour or alarming news, including through electronic means, with intent to create or promote, or which 
is likely to create or promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or 
community or any other ground whatsoever, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different 
religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with 
imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.

(d) makes or publishes false or misleading information, jeopardising the sovereignty, unity and 
integrity or security of India, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (1) in any place of worship or in any 
assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished 
with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.

intention, is done by several persons, each of such persons who joins in the act with such knowledge or

or intention.

omission, is an offence, it is to be understood that the causing of that effect partly by an act and partly by 
an omission is the same offence.

A has committed murder.

commission of that offence by doing any one of those acts, either singly or jointly with any other person,

(a) A and B agree to murder Z by severally and at different times giving him small doses of poison. 
A and B administer the poison according to the agreement with intent to murder Z. Z dies from the 
effects the several doses of poison so administered to him. Here A and B intentionally cooperate in the 
commission of murder and as each of them does an act by which the death is caused, they are both guilty 
of the offence though their acts are separate. 
(b) A and B are joint jailors, and as such have the charge of Z, a prisoner, alternatively for six hours 
at a time. A and B, intending to cause Z’s death, knowingly cooperate in causing that effect by illegally 
omitting, each during the time of his attendance, to furnish Z with food supplied to them for that purpose. 
Z dies of hunger. Both A and B are guilty of the murder of Z. 
(c) A, a jailor, has the charge of Z, a prisoner. A, intending to cause Z’s death, illegally omits to 
supply Z with food; in consequence of which Z is much reduced in strength, but the starvation is not 
sufficient to cause his death. A is dismissed from his office, and B succeeds him. B, without collusion or 
cooperation with A, illegally omits to supply Z with food, knowing that he is likely thereby to cause Z’s 
death. Z dies of hunger. B is guilty of murder, but, as A did not cooperate with B. A is guilty only of an 
attempt to commit murder.

guilty of different offences by means of that act.

culpable homicide not amounting to murder. B, having ill-will towards Z and intending to kill him, and 
not having been subject to the provocation, assists A in killing Z. Here, though A and B are both engaged

Further, it is requested to inquire into the matter under Section 59 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to determine whether the neighbour's actions constituted an "act intended to provoke a breach of peace" (Article 59.1.2), thereby warranting preventive action to maintain public tranquility.

Additionally, it is necessary to ascertain the veracity of the allegations and gather evidence in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), particularly Article 5.2.1 which deals with the admissibility of hearsay evidence, and Article 13.1.1 which pertains to the examination of witnesses.

## Summary

The applicant is seeking redressal under Section 293 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for the alleged commission of the offence of "Injuring or defiling places of worship, or religious rites of the deceased, etc. - causing affront to the dignity of an individual". The neighbour allegedly insulted the applicant in front of the entire colony, trying to provoke a fight. The applicant also requests an inquiry into the matter under Section 59 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 to determine whether the neighbour's actions constituted an "act intended to provoke a breach of peace".

## Applicable BNS provisions

[BNS Section 293] Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (specifically, Article 293.1.1 and Article 293.1.2)
[BNS Section 59] Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (specifically, Article 59.1.2)
[BNS Section 5] Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 
[BNS Section 197] Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 
[BNS Section 196] Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 
[BNS Section 299] Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 
[BNS Section 301] Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 
[BNS Section 57] Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 
[BNS Section 4] Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 
[BNS Section 1] Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 

## Recommendation / next steps

Considering the allegations, it is recommended to initiate an inquiry under Section 59 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 to determine whether the neighbour's actions constituted an "act intended to provoke a breach of peace". The inquiry should also gather evidence in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, particularly Article 5.2.1 which deals with the admissibility of hearsay evidence, and Article 13.1.1 which pertains to the examination of witnesses.

If the neighbour is found guilty, appropriate action should be taken under Section 293 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, including prosecution and punishment as per the relevant provisions.

commission of that offence by doing any one of those acts, either singly or jointly with any other person, 
commits that offence.

A and B administer the poison according to the agreement with intent to murder Z. Z dies from the 
effects the several doses of poison so administered to him. Here A and B intentionally cooperate in the 
commission of murder and as each of them does an act by which the death is caused, they are both guilty 
of the offence though their acts are separate. 
(b) A and B are joint jailors, and as such have the charge of Z, a prisoner, alternatively for six hours 
at a time. A and B, intending to cause Z’s death, knowingly cooperate in causing that effect by illegally 
omitting, each during the time of his attendance, to furnish Z with food supplied to them for that purpose. 
Z dies of hunger. Both A and B are guilty of the murder of Z. 
(c) A, a jailor, has the charge of Z, a prisoner. A, intending to cause Z’s death, illegally omits to 
supply Z with food; in consequence of which Z is much reduced in strength, but the starvation is not 
sufficient to cause his death. A is dismissed from his office, and B succeeds him. B, without collusion or 
cooperation with A, illegally omits to supply Z with food, knowing that he is likely thereby to cause Z’s 
death. Z dies of hunger. B is guilty of murder, but, as A did not cooperate with B. A is guilty only of an 
attempt to commit murder.

guilty of different offences by means of that act.

culpable homicide not amounting to murder. B, having ill-will towards Z and intending to kill him, and 
not having been subject to the provocation, assists A in killing Z. Here, though A and B are both engaged 
in causing Z’s death, B is guilty of murder, and A is guilty only of culpable homicide.

Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I seek guidance on the following:

Does the operation of a printing press in my area, producing notes bearing the denomination of two-thousand rupees without authority, constitute an offence under Article 294 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023?

Further, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, what are the powers and procedures available to the law enforcement agency to seize the printing press and the counterfeit currency, and initiate proceedings against the perpetrators?

Additionally, what is the admissibility of the evidence collected from the printing press, including documents, machinery, and physical materials, as per the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, specifically Article 47(3) thereof?
result.answer:
## Summary

The operation of a printing press in your area, producing notes bearing the denomination of two-thousand rupees without authority, constitutes an offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023. The production of counterfeit currency is a serious offence that can be punishable under various sections of BNS_2023.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 178] Counterfeiting coin, Government stamps, currency-notes or bank-notes.
- [BNS Section 179] Using as genuine, forged or counterfeit coin, Government stamp, currency-notes or bank-notes.
- [BNS Section 180] Possession of forged or counterfeit coin, Government stamp, currency-notes or bank-notes.

## Recommendation / next steps

As the production of counterfeit currency is a serious offence, the law enforcement agency should take immediate action to seize the printing press and the counterfeit currency. The agency should also initiate proceedings against the perpetrators under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

The admissibility of evidence collected from the printing press, including documents, machinery, and physical materials, is governed by the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023. The law enforcement agency should ensure that the evidence is collected and preserved in accordance with the provisions of the Act.

The specific powers and procedures available to the law enforcement agency to seize the printing press and the counterfeit currency, and initiate proceedings against the perpetrators, are governed by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023. The agency should act in accordance with the provisions of the Act to ensure a fair and effective investigation.

This petition prays that an investigation be conducted pursuant to Article 35 of the BNSS, against the respondent who has allegedly committed the offence of making/use of forged document, contrary to Article 234 of the BNS, by presenting a forged court order at the registrar's office in order to claim ownership of the petitioner's ancestral property, thus committing the offence of false imputation of title under Article 237 of the BNS.

The petitioner prays that an inquiry be conducted under Article 20 of the BNSS and that the respondent be summoned to face trial for the aforementioned offences.

Verification of authenticity of the document presented by the respondent and the title of the property in question may be conducted under Article 17 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) to determine the truth and correctness of the allegations.

The petitioner humbly submits that the respondent's actions are a serious breach of Article 123 of the BNSS, which pertains to the maintenance of public order and tranquility.

The petition is made under Article 14 of the BNSS, seeking the intervention of this Honorable Court to ensure justice and protect the petitioner's rights under the law.

Verification of relevant documents, including the record of the property and the court order presented by the respondent, be conducted under Article 24 of the BSA, to ascertain the truth and correctness of the allegations.

intention, is done by several persons, each of such persons who joins in the act with such knowledge or 
intention is liable for the act in the same manner as if the act were done by him alone with that knowledge 
or intention.

commission of murder and as each of them does an act by which the death is caused, they are both guilty

death. Z dies of hunger. B is guilty of murder, but, as A did not cooperate with B. A is guilty only of an 
attempt to commit murder.

## Summary

The complainant alleges that a fake will was created in the name of their deceased father, with forged signatures of the deceased and a witness, with the intention of claiming the property. The complainant requests an investigation, identification of the perpetrator(s), collection of evidence, and prosecution under Section 415 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 337] Forgery of record of Court or of public register, etc.
- [BNS Section 336] Forgery
- [BNS Section 415] Punishment for Cheating
- [BNS Section 339] Punishment for having possession of forged document or electronic record
- [BNS Section 335] Making a false document
- [BNS Section 230] Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence

## Recommendation / next steps

Based on the information provided, it appears that the complainant has a strong case against the perpetrator(s) involved in creating the fake will. The applicable BNS provisions suggest that the perpetrator(s) may be liable for forgery, cheating, and other related offenses.

I recommend that the authorities conduct a thorough investigation into the creation and submission of the forged will, and collect evidence related to the forged signatures and the will. The perpetrator(s) should be identified and prosecuted under the relevant BNS provisions.

Additionally, the authorities should verify the execution of the will and the authenticity of the signatures to determine the legitimacy of the will. If the will is found to be forged, the authorities should take steps to rectify the situation and ensure that the property is transferred to the rightful heirs.

It is also recommended that the authorities inform the complainant about the progress of the investigation and the next steps to be taken in the case. The complainant should be kept updated on the investigation and be informed of any developments or changes in the case.

not having been subject to the provocation, assists A in killing Z. Here, though A and B are both engaged 
in causing Z’s death, B is guilty of murder, and A is guilty only of culpable homicide.

Pursuant to Article 123(1)(i) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is requested that a thorough investigation be conducted into the allegations of Section 123(2) - 'Using forged documents to execute agreements' against the shopkeeper, and the relevant provisions of Article 123(3) be invoked to initiate appropriate legal action. 

Additionally, under Article 45(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), the local magistrate is requested to proceed under Section 45(2) to gather evidence, and Article 45(5) to summon the shopkeeper for questioning, in order to ascertain the truth of the allegations and ensure the safety and security of the public. 

Furthermore, under Article 27(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), all relevant documents and evidence, including the fake stamp papers, be collected and preserved as per the provisions of Section 27(2) to be used as evidence in the ensuing legal proceedings, and the burden of proof under Article 27(3) be established to determine the guilt or innocence of the shopkeeper.

The burden of proof under Article 27(3) of the BSA should be established to determine the guilt or innocence of the shopkeeper.

intention is liable for the act in the same manner as if the act were done by him alone with that knowledge 
or intention. 
(7) Wherever the causing of a certain effect, or an attempt to cause that effect, by an act or by an 
omission, is an offence, it is to be understood that the causing of that effect partly by an act and partly by 
an omission is the same offence. 
A intentionally causes Z’s death, partly by illegally omitting to give Z food, and partly by beating Z. 
A has committed murder. 
(8) When an offence is committed by means of several acts, whoever intentionally cooperates in the 
commission of that offence by doing any one of those acts, either singly or jointly with any other person, 
commits that offence. 
(a) A and B agree to murder Z by severally and at different times giving him small doses of poison. 
A and B administer the poison according to the agreement with intent to murder Z. Z dies from the 
effects the several doses of poison so administered to him. Here A and B intentionally cooperate in the 
commission of murder and as each of them does an act by which the death is caused, they are both guilty 
of the offence though their acts are separate. 
(b) A and B are joint jailors, and as such have the charge of Z, a prisoner, alternatively for six hours 
at a time. A and B, intending to cause Z’s death, knowingly cooperate in causing that effect by illegally 
omitting, each during the time of his attendance, to furnish Z with food supplied to them for that purpose. 
Z dies of hunger. Both A and B are guilty of the murder of Z. 
(c) A, a jailor, has the charge of Z, a prisoner. A, intending to cause Z’s death, illegally omits to 
supply Z with food; in consequence of which Z is much reduced in strength, but the starvation is not 
sufficient to cause his death. A is dismissed from his office, and B succeeds him. B, without collusion or 
cooperation with A, illegally omits to supply Z with food, knowing that he is likely thereby to cause Z’s 
death. Z dies of hunger. B is guilty of murder, but, as A did not cooperate with B. A is guilty only of an 
attempt to commit murder. 
(9) Where several persons are engaged or concerned in the commission of a criminal act, they may be 
guilty of different offences by means of that act. 
A attacks Z under such circumstances of grave provocation that his killing of Z would be only 
culpable homicide not amounting to murder. B, having ill-will towards Z and intending to kill him, and 
not having been subject to the provocation, assists A in killing Z. Here, though A and B are both engaged 
in causing Z’s death, B is guilty of murder, and A is guilty only of culpable homicide.

Pursuant to Article 32 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is requested that a legal opinion be provided on the following scenario:

A person, identified as a 'drug peddler' under the BNS, was apprehended while selling 'scheduled substances' as defined under BNS, in close proximity to an educational institution. During the course of the arrest, it was discovered that the accused was in possession of a licensed firearm, which was allegedly used to intimidate 'debtors' who had failed to settle their obligations with the accused, thereby violating Article 67 of the BNS.

In light of these facts, please advise on the applicable provisions of the BNS and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) regarding the charge sheet to be filed against the accused, and the admissibility of evidence, as per the guidelines outlined in the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).
result.answer:
## Summary

The accused, a 'drug peddler,' has been apprehended for selling 'scheduled substances' near a school and found in possession of a licensed firearm that was allegedly used to intimidate 'debtors.' These actions violate the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS).

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 113] deals with terrorist acts, which may be applicable due to the use of a firearm to intimidate debtors. 
- [BNS Section 148] pertains to conspiracy to commit offences, which could be relevant in this case. 
- [BNS Section 278] addresses the sale of drugs as a different drug or preparation, which directly applies to the accused's actions. 
- [BNS Section 149] deals with collecting arms with the intention of waging war against the Government of India, which might be relevant due to the licensed firearm's use in intimidation. 
- [BNS Section 209] pertains to non-appearance in response to a proclamation, which might be applicable in case of the accused's non-cooperation during the investigation.

## Recommendation / next steps

Considering the above points, the charge sheet against the accused should include charges under [BNS Section 113] for terrorist acts, [BNS Section 148] for conspiracy, [BNS Section 278] for selling scheduled substances, and [BNS Section 149] for using a firearm to intimidate debtors. Additionally, if the accused fails to cooperate with the investigation or appears at the specified place and time as required by a proclamation, he may be charged under [BNS Section 209].

of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

Punishment for false evidence.—(1) Whoever intentionally gives false evidence in any stage 
of a judicial proceeding, or fabricates false evidence for the purpose of being used in any stage of a 
judicial proceeding, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may 
extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees. 
(2) Whoever intentionally gives or fabricates false evidence in any case other than that referred to in 
sub-section (1), shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 
three years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to five thousand rupees. 
Explanation 1.—A trial before a Court-martial is a judicial proceeding. 
Explanation 2.—An investigation directed by law preliminary to a proceeding before a Court, is a 
stage of a judicial proceeding, though that investigation may not take place before a Court. 
A, in an enquiry before a Magistrate for the purpose of ascertaining whether Z ought to be committed

proceeding, A has given false evidence.

authority of a Court, is a stage of a judicial proceeding, though that investigation may not take place 
before a Court.

makes on oath a statement which he knows to be false. As this enquiry is a stage of a judicial proceeding, 
A has given false evidence.

Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence.—

he will thereby cause, any person to be convicted of an offence which is capital by the law for the time 
being in force in India shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a 
term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to fifty thousand 
rupees. 
(2) If an innocent person be convicted and executed in consequence of false evidence referred to in 
sub-section (1), the person who gives such false evidence shall be punished either with death or the 
punishment specified in sub-section (1).

Statements conducing to public mischief.—(1) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any 
statement, false information, rumour, or report, including through electronic means— 
(a) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the 
Army, Navy or Air Force of India to mutiny or otherwise disregard or fail in his duty as such; or 
(b) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, fear or alarm to the public, or to any section 
of the public whereby any person may be induced to commit an offence against the State or against 
the public tranquillity; or 
(c) with intent to incite, or which is likely to incite, any class or community of persons to commit 
any offence against any other class or community, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement or report containing false information, 
rumour or alarming news, including through electronic means, with intent to create or promote, or which 
is likely to create or promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or 
community or any other ground whatsoever, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different 
religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with 
imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(3) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (2) in any place of worship or in any 
assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished 
with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine. 
Exception.—It does not amount to an offence, within the meaning of this section, when the person 
making, publishing or circulating any such statement, false information, rumour or report, has reasonable 
grounds for believing that such statement, false information, rumour or report is true and makes, 
publishes or circulates it in good faith and without any such intent as aforesaid.

Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147.—Whoever within or without and 
beyond India conspires to commit any of the offences punishable by section 147, or conspires to 
overawe, by means of criminal force or the show of criminal force, the Central Government or any State 
Government, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description 
which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. 
Explanation.—To constitute a conspiracy under this section, it is not necessary that any act or illegal 
omission shall take place in pursuance thereof.

effects the several doses of poison so administered to him. Here A and B intentionally cooperate in the 
commission of murder and as each of them does an act by which the death is caused, they are both guilty

omitting, each during the time of his attendance, to furnish Z with food supplied to them for that purpose.

cooperation with A, illegally omits to supply Z with food, knowing that he is likely thereby to cause Z’s

Punishment for false evidence.—(1) Whoever intentionally gives false evidence in any stage

sub-section (1), shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 
three years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to five thousand rupees.

proceeding, A has given false evidence.

## Summary

The petition seeks an investigation and prosecution into the alleged commission of several offences committed during a communal riot, including arson, rioting with deadly weapons, gang rape, and causing grievous hurt. The petition also requests the invocation of provisions for the immediate apprehension and detention of the accused, seizure of evidence, preservation of the crime scene, collection and preservation of evidence, and examination of the victim and other relevant witnesses.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 1] (definition of an offence)
- [BNS Section 4] (overview of the new law)
- [BNS Section 195] (assaulting or obstructing a public servant when suppressing a riot)
- [BNS Section 52] (abettor when liable to cumulative punishment for act abetted and for act done)
- [BNS Section 209] (non-appearance in response to a proclamation)
- [BNS Section 148] (conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147)
- [BNS Section 192] (wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot-if rioting be committed; if not committed)

## Recommendation / next steps

Grant the petition and initiate an investigation into the alleged commission of the offences of arson, rioting with deadly weapons, gang rape, and causing grievous hurt. Also, invoke the provisions of Article 19(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 for the immediate apprehension and detention of the accused, and Article 23(3) for the seizure of evidence and preservation of the crime scene. Collect and preserve evidence, particularly the testimony of the victim, and examine the victim and other relevant witnesses according to the provisions of Article 17(1) and 24(2) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023.

We respectfully submit a formal complaint under Article 6, Section 1 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) against the perpetrators of the terrorist attack that occurred on [date] at the market in [location]. We request investigation and examination of all available evidence under Article 22, Section 3 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) to ascertain the identity and culpability of the perpetrators. We further request that the investigating agency take all necessary measures to recover the explosive materials and other evidence under Article 15, Section 4 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

We also request that the investigating agency examine the possibility of conspiracy under Article 17, Section 2 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and gather evidence to support the charges under Article 18, Section 3 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

We respectfully request that the investigating agency expedite the investigation and submit a report under Article 30, Section 2 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to enable the prosecution to proceed with the case under Article 25, Section 1 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

A terrorist group has planted a bomb in a market, killing five people and injuring dozens. A complaint has been filed under Article 6, Section 1 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) against the perpetrators, requesting an investigation and examination of all available evidence. The investigating agency is also asked to examine the possibility of conspiracy and gather evidence to support charges. The complainant seeks an expedited investigation to enable the prosecution to proceed with the case.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 113]
- [BNS Section 148]
- [BNS Section 46]

## Recommendation / next steps

Based on the provided context, it appears that the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) provides specific provisions for dealing with terrorist acts and conspiracies. The investigating agency is required to take necessary measures to recover explosive materials and other evidence related to the terrorist attack, as per Article 15, Section 4 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

The complaint filed under Article 6, Section 1 of the BNS should be investigated thoroughly, and the possibility of conspiracy should be examined under [BNS Section 148]. Any person found to be involved in the terrorist act or conspiracy should be punished accordingly, as per the provisions of [BNS Section 113].

It is also essential to note that [BNS Section 46] clarifies the concept of conspiracy, stating that it is sufficient for a person to engage in a conspiracy in pursuance of which the offence is committed. This provision may be relevant in the investigation process to determine the extent of involvement of the perpetrators.

In light of the above, the next steps would be to ensure a thorough investigation, gather evidence, and take necessary actions to prosecute the perpetrators under the relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

which refer to acts done extend also to illegal omissions. 
(5) When a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, 
each of such persons is liable for that act in the same manner as if it were done by him alone. 
(6) Whenever an act, which is criminal only by reason of its being done with a criminal knowledge or 
intention, is done by several persons, each of such persons who joins in the act with such knowledge or 
intention is liable for the act in the same manner as if the act were done by him alone with that knowledge 
or intention. 
(7) Wherever the causing of a certain effect, or an attempt to cause that effect, by an act or by an 
omission, is an offence, it is to be understood that the causing of that effect partly by an act and partly by 
an omission is the same offence. 
A intentionally causes Z’s death, partly by illegally omitting to give Z food, and partly by beating Z. 
A has committed murder. 
(8) When an offence is committed by means of several acts, whoever intentionally cooperates in the 
commission of that offence by doing any one of those acts, either singly or jointly with any other person, 
commits that offence. 
(a) A and B agree to murder Z by severally and at different times giving him small doses of poison. 
A and B administer the poison according to the agreement with intent to murder Z. Z dies from the 
effects the several doses of poison so administered to him. Here A and B intentionally cooperate in the 
commission of murder and as each of them does an act by which the death is caused, they are both guilty 
of the offence though their acts are separate. 
(b) A and B are joint jailors, and as such have the charge of Z, a prisoner, alternatively for six hours 
at a time. A and B, intending to cause Z’s death, knowingly cooperate in causing that effect by illegally 
omitting, each during the time of his attendance, to furnish Z with food supplied to them for that purpose. 
Z dies of hunger. Both A and B are guilty of the murder of Z. 
(c) A, a jailor, has the charge of Z, a prisoner. A, intending to cause Z’s death, illegally omits to 
supply Z with food; in consequence of which Z is much reduced in strength, but the starvation is not 
sufficient to cause his death. A is dismissed from his office, and B succeeds him. B, without collusion or 
cooperation with A, illegally omits to supply Z with food, knowing that he is likely thereby to cause Z’s 
death. Z dies of hunger. B is guilty of murder, but, as A did not cooperate with B. A is guilty only of an 
attempt to commit murder.

guilty of different offences by means of that act.

not having been subject to the provocation, assists A in killing Z. Here, though A and B are both engaged 
in causing Z’s death, B is guilty of murder, and A is guilty only of culpable homicide.

act or acquired through the commission of any terrorist act shall be punished with imprisonment for a 
term which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. 
Explanation.—For the removal of doubts, it is hereby declared that the officer not below the rank of 
Superintendent of Police shall decide whether to register the case under this section or under the

Abettor.—A person abets an offence, who abets either the commission of an offence, or the 
commission of an act which would be an offence, if committed by a person capable by law of committing 
an offence with the same intention or knowledge as that of the abettor. 
Explanation 1.—The abetment of the illegal omission of an act may amount to an offence although 
the abettor may not himself be bound to do that act. 
Explanation 2.—To constitute the offence of abetment it is not necessary that the act abetted should 
be committed, or that the effect requisite to constitute the offence should be caused. 
(a) A instigates B to murder C. B refuses to do so. A is guilty of abetting B to commit murder. 
(b) A instigates B to murder D. B in pursuance of the instigation stabs D. D recovers from the wound. 
A is guilty of instigating B to commit murder. 
Explanation 3.—It is not necessary that the person abetted should be capable by law of committing 
an offence, or that he should have the same guilty intention or knowledge as that of the abettor, or any 
guilty intention or knowledge. 
(a) A, with a guilty intention, abets a child or a person of unsound mind to commit an act which 
would be an offence, if committed by a person capable by law of committing an offence, and having the 
same intention as A. Here A, whether the act be committed or not, is guilty of abetting an offence. 
(b) A, with the intention of murdering Z, instigates B, a child under seven years of age, to do an act 
which causes Z’s death. B, in consequence of the abetment, does the act in the absence of A and thereby 
causes Z’s death. Here, though B was not capable by law of committing an offence, A is liable to be 
punished in the same manner as if B had been capable by law of committing an offence, and had 
committed murder, and he is therefore subject to the punishment of death. 
(c) A instigates B to set fire to a dwelling-house. B, in consequence of his unsoundness of mind, 
being incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is wrong or contrary to law, sets 
fire to the house in consequence of A’s instigation. B has committed no offence, but A is guilty of 
abetting the offence of setting fire to a dwelling-house, and is liable to the punishment provided for that 
(d) A, intending to cause a theft to be committed, instigates B to take property belonging to Z out of 
Z’s possession. A induces B to believe that the property belongs to A. B takes the property out of Z’s 
possession, in good faith, believing it to be A’s property. B, acting under this misconception, does not 
take dishonestly, and therefore does not commit theft. But A is guilty of abetting theft, and is liable to the 
same punishment as if B had committed theft. 
Explanation 4.—The abetment of an offence being an offence, the abetment of such an abetment is 
also an offence. 
A instigates B to instigate C to murder Z. B accordingly instigates C to murder Z, and C commits that 
offence in consequence of B’s instigation. B is liable to be punished for his offence with the punishment 
for murder; and, as A instigated B to commit the offence, A is also liable to the same punishment. 
Explanation 5.—It is not necessary to the commission of the offence of abetment by conspiracy that 
the abettor should concert the offence with the person who commits it. It is sufficient if he engages in the 
conspiracy in pursuance of which the offence is committed.

A concerts with B a plan for poisoning Z. It is agreed that A shall administer the poison. B then 
explains the plan to C mentioning that a third person is to administer the poison, but without mentioning 
A’s name. C agrees to procure the poison, and procures and delivers it to B for the purpose of its being 
used in the manner explained. A administers the poison; Z dies in consequence. Here, though A and C 
have not conspired together, yet C has been engaged in the conspiracy in pursuance of which Z has been 
murdered. C has therefore committed the offence defined in this section and is liable to the punishment 
for murder.

Specifically, the doctor allegedly engaged in a coercive act by demanding payment as a prerequisite for medical treatment, in contravention of the provisions of the BNS dealing with undue influence and extortion. 

Further, the actions of the doctor have been alleged to be in violation of Article 127 of the BNS, which pertains to the duty of healthcare professionals to provide emergency medical aid without discrimination or prejudice.

In light of these allegations, it is requested to determine whether the doctor has committed an offence under the BNS, and if so, whether any other provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) or the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) are applicable to this case.

## Summary
A doctor employed at a government hospital has been accused of attempting to extort money (Rs 50,000) from a poor patient's family in exchange for performing an emergency surgery. The doctor allegedly engaged in coercive acts by demanding payment as a prerequisite for medical treatment, violating provisions related to undue influence and extortion under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 308] - Extortion
- [BNS Section 200] - Punishment for non-treatment of victim
- [BNS Section 314] - Criminal breach of trust
- [BNS Section 245] - Fraudulently suffering decree for sum not due
- [BNS Section 106] - Causing death by negligence (Although not directly relevant, this provision might be applicable in case of a severe consequence arising from the doctor's actions)

## Recommendation / next steps
Considering the allegations, the doctor's actions may fall under the provisions related to extortion, non-treatment of victims, and possibly criminal breach of trust. Further investigation is required to determine the extent of the doctor's culpability and the specific laws that have been violated. The case may be referred to a court for a thorough examination and determination of the applicable laws and the consequent punishment.

Pursuant to the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), the following legal query is raised:

Whether the act of a woman, who, with the intention to cause the death of her husband, mixed poison into his food, amounts to the offence under Article 123(BNS), read with Article 124(BNS), and whether the fact that the husband survived the poisoning is relevant to the determination of the above offence? 

Furthermore, whether the taking of a large life insurance policy by the woman on her husband, one week prior to the incident, constitutes a relevant circumstance under Article 35(BNS) of the abovementioned Act, which may be considered during the investigation and trial of the said case?

Additionally, under the provisions of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), whether the statements made by the woman to the investigating agency, regarding her intentions and actions, are admissible as evidence under Article 20(BSA), and whether the evidence of the insurance policy taken by her, is relevant and admissible under Article 27(BSA) of the said Act?

## Summary
A woman intentionally mixed poison into her husband's food with the intention to cause his death. Although her husband survived, the woman had also taken a large life insurance policy on him a week prior to the incident. We need to determine if her actions amount to the offence under Article 123(BNS) read with Article 124(BNS). Additionally, we need to consider if the taking of the life insurance policy constitutes a relevant circumstance under Article 35(BNS). Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), we need to evaluate if the statements made by the woman regarding her intentions and actions are admissible as evidence under Article 20(BSA), and if the evidence of the insurance policy is relevant and admissible under Article 27(BSA).

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 1]
- [BNS Section 90]
- [BNS Section 46]
- [BNS Section 51]
- [BNS Section 109]
- [BNS Section 106]
- [BNS Section 123]
- [BNS Section 124]
- [BNS Section 35]

## Recommendation / next steps
Given the circumstances of the case, it appears that the woman's actions may amount to the offence under Article 123(BNS) read with Article 124(BNS). The fact that the husband survived does not necessarily affect the determination of the offence, as the woman's intention was to cause his death. Additionally, the taking of the life insurance policy on her husband a week prior to the incident may be considered a relevant circumstance under Article 35(BNS).

Regarding the admissibility of evidence, the statements made by the woman regarding her intentions and actions may be admissible as evidence under Article 20(BSA), as they are relevant to the investigation and trial of the case. However, the evidence of the insurance policy may be relevant and admissible under Article 27(BSA) only if it is shown to be a material fact in the case.

To proceed with the investigation and trial, the relevant authorities should gather more evidence and consider the applicable BNS provisions. The woman's statements and the life insurance policy may be used as evidence in determining the offence and her liability.

the abettor should concert the offence with the person who commits it. It is sufficient if he engages in the 
conspiracy in pursuance of which the offence is committed.

A concerts with B a plan for poisoning Z. It is agreed that A shall administer the poison. B then 
explains the plan to C mentioning that a third person is to administer the poison, but without mentioning 
A’s name. C agrees to procure the poison, and procures and delivers it to B for the purpose of its being 
used in the manner explained. A administers the poison; Z dies in consequence. Here, though A and C 
have not conspired together, yet C has been engaged in the conspiracy in pursuance of which Z has been 
murdered. C has therefore committed the offence defined in this section and is liable to the punishment 
for murder.

## Summary

A Dalit family was subjected to severe physical harm, destruction of their household items, and casteist slurs by a group of men in a village setting. This incident has raised concerns about violations of several provisions under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS_2023). The complainant has submitted a request for investigation into the alleged commission of various offenses.

## Applicable BNS provisions

[BNS Section 321](1)(a) - Cruelty by a group of individuals
[BNS Section 325](2)(a) - Intentional destruction of property
[BNS Section 328](3)(b) - Incitement to caste-based animosity
[BNS Section 335](1)(a) - Unlawful assembly and rioting
[BNS Section 57 - Abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons]
[BNS Section 353 - Statements conducing to public mischief]
[BNS Section 299 - Deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs]

## Recommendation / next steps

A thorough investigation into the alleged offenses should be conducted, and necessary action be taken against the perpetrators under the provisions of BNS. Relevant evidence should be collected and preserved in accordance with the procedures prescribed under [BNS Section 150]. The public servants or officials who failed to prevent the commission of the aforesaid offenses should also be held accountable for their inaction under [BNS Section 245](5) - Failure to prevent commission of a crime.
